PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single behavior with a single Arrange-Act-Assert.
RATIONALE: Atomic tests isolate failures and make diagnosis easy.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for number of distinct Act operations; multiple unrelated operations indicate non-compliance.
DECISION RULES: The method performs a single call to MaxMin4.maxMin4(...) (one Act) and asserts the exception and array post-conditions; no other methods are tested.
VERDICT: compliant — the test focuses on a single behavior (out-of-range 'to' index) with one Act and related assertions.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests or shared mutable state.
RATIONALE: Independence enables arbitrary execution order and parallelism.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Check for @Before/@After usage, shared mutable static/instance state, or numbered test names.
DECISION RULES: The test uses only local variables (intArray0) and no static or instance fields; no evidence of dependence on other tests or ordered naming.
VERDICT: compliant — test is self-contained and does not rely on external/shared mutable state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: For each method being tested, include happy-path and error-path tests.
RATIONALE: Verifying both normal and exceptional flows increases confidence and robustness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: The class should provide at least two tests per method: a success (happy path) and an error scenario; look for @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows.
DECISION RULES: The test class contains only a single test method (test0) exercising an exceptional flow; there is no separate happy-path test in the provided code.
VERDICT: non-compliant — only an exceptional-case test is present and no normal/happy-path test exists for MaxMin4.maxMin4 in the shown class.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary and out-of-range inputs.
RATIONALE: Boundaries are frequent sources of bugs (off-by-one, range checks).
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for use of 0, -1, large out-of-range values, empty arrays, Integer.MAX_VALUE, or names indicating boundary tests.
DECISION RULES: The test supplies a 'to' index (3137) that is well beyond the array length and uses 0 as the from index; this intentionally exercises an out-of-range boundary condition.
VERDICT: compliant — the test explicitly targets an out-of-range boundary scenario for indices.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and avoid duplication via helper methods/constants.
RATIONALE: Modularity reduces duplication and improves maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for helper methods, constants, or duplicated code across tests; very short independent tests can be acceptable.
DECISION RULES: The class has only one short test and no duplicated blocks across multiple tests; though no helpers/constants are present, there is no evidence of duplication or lack of modularity given the single test.
VERDICT: compliant — the test is self-contained and not duplicated across methods in the shown snippet.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and low-complexity (no loops or complex conditionals).
RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to verify and maintain.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Check for method length (>30 lines), loops, or nested conditionals.
DECISION RULES: The test method is short (well under 30 lines), contains no loops or complex conditionals and follows a linear Arrange-Act-Assert flow with a try/catch for the expected exception.
VERDICT: compliant — test is small and simple with low cyclomatic complexity.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive and check relevant properties, not only superficial conditions.
RATIONALE: Multiple assertions increase the chance of detecting faults.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Multiple assertions verifying more than a single property are preferred (e.g., multiple fields or collection size + contents).
DECISION RULES: The test asserts that a specific array element retains its value and that the array length remains unchanged (two distinct properties), rather than just doing assertNotNull or a single superficial check.
VERDICT: compliant — multiple meaningful assertions are used to validate post-conditions.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled and commented-out tests; keep tests runnable.
RATIONALE: Ignored or commented tests hide unfinished work or regressions.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test methods.
DECISION RULES: No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out test methods appear in the provided code; the test is active and runnable (has @Test).
VERDICT: compliant — the test is active and not disabled or commented out.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be traceable to requirements via annotations or Javadoc.
RATIONALE: Traceability enables mapping tests to requirements for impact analysis.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Story/@Requirement annotations or Javadoc references like REQ-/US-/JIRA-.
DECISION RULES: The class-level Javadoc includes Traceability lines referencing REQ-001, REQ-002, and REQ-003, directly linking tests to requirements.
VERDICT: compliant — the class contains explicit Javadoc requirement IDs for traceability.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be explicit and separate; unit tests typically do not cover them unless annotated.
RATIONALE: Non-functional tests are important and should be clearly identified.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Test(timeout=...) or explicit performance/security test code.
DECISION RULES: Although unit tests often mark this practice as not-applicable, this test uses @Test(timeout = 4000) which is an explicit timeout-based constraint that qualifies as a basic performance-related assertion.
VERDICT: compliant — the presence of an explicit @Test timeout indicates an awareness of execution time constraints and meets the narrow criteria for this practice.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome.
RATIONALE: Descriptive names make tests self-documenting and failures easier to interpret.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Names should follow patterns like methodName_condition_expectedResult; generic names like test0 are non-compliant.
DECISION RULES: The test method is named test0, which is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected behavior.
VERDICT: non-compliant — the method name is not descriptive; it should be renamed to convey its intent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Avoid heavy auto-generated, verbose test code and auto-generated names.
RATIONALE: Generated tests often have generic names (test0) and tool-specific imports that reduce readability and maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for auto-generated comments, tool-specific imports (e.g., EvoSuite), or repetitive auto-generated names like test0/test1.
DECISION RULES: The class includes imports from org.evosuite.runtime and uses a test method named test0 — both strong signals of tool-generated code.
VERDICT: non-compliant — evidence of EvoSuite-generated patterns (imports and generic method name) indicates heavy code-generation artifacts.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should show evidence of thoughtful design such as Given-When-Then or BDD naming.
RATIONALE: Well-designed tests (TDD/BDD) are more comprehensive and maintainable.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style names; coverage of multiple scenarios is also evidence of design intent.
DECISION RULES: The class-level Javadoc and the test method include Given/When/Then comments, indicating a deliberate design approach even though only one test is present.
VERDICT: compliant — the presence of Given-When-Then structure in comments indicates prioritized test design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should verify behavior via public APIs and avoid coupling to internal implementation.
RATIONALE: Tests that depend on internals are brittle and increase maintenance burden.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for reflection, checking private fields, or tightly coupled internal checks.
DECISION RULES: The test uses the public API MaxMin4.maxMin4(...) and does not use reflection or access private members; it verifies observable behavior (exception thrown and array unchanged).
VERDICT: compliant — the test focuses on public behavior and does not rely on implementation internals.

PRINCIPLE: Use clear, specific assertions with messages when helpful.
RATIONALE: Descriptive assertions improve failure diagnostics.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Prefer assertEquals/assertThat with messages over generic assertTrue; presence of messages is a positive signal.
DECISION RULES: The test uses assertEquals with descriptive messages for both checks, avoiding generic assertions.
VERDICT: compliant — assertions are specific and include descriptive messages.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' not 'what'; avoid excessive or commented-out code.
RATIONALE: Useful comments aid maintenance; excessive comments lead to confusion.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for commented-out code or >50% comment density; Given-When-Then comments are acceptable.
DECISION RULES: The test includes brief Given/When/Then comments and no commented-out code; comments add structure rather than restating code.
VERDICT: compliant — comments are minimal and informative, not excessive.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must avoid sources of non-determinism (randomness, time, external deps) unless mocked/seeds used.
RATIONALE: Deterministic tests prevent flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Search for Random(), Math.random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep(), or external calls without mocking.
DECISION RULES: The test uses only deterministic local data and no randomness, time-based calls, or sleeps; no external dependencies are present in the snippet.
VERDICT: compliant — test is deterministic and free of non-deterministic constructs.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should not leave persistent side effects or modify shared global state.
RATIONALE: Side effects create inter-test dependencies and flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for file/database writes, static modifications, or missing cleanup when resources are created.
DECISION RULES: The test operates on a locally created int[] and does not modify static variables or external resources; no cleanup is required.
VERDICT: compliant — no side effects or shared-state modifications are present.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories

RATIONALE: Labels allow running subsets (unit/integration/smoke) and improve CI efficiency.
